name: Akhand Bharat
summary: Akhand Bharat, or undivided India, is the irredentist idea that the Indian subcontinent is one civilisational homeland and should be one nation, reversing the 1947 Partition. It belongs to the Hindutva family, with the RSS, Hindu Mahasabha and Jana Sangh as its main carriers. Today's mainstream says reunification should come by popular goodwill rather than conquest.
scope: The Hindutva-linked Akhand Bharat position as held by the Sangh family: Savarkar's Essentials of Hindutva (1923), Golwalkar, the Jana Sangh programme and later RSS statements (Bhagwat, Ram Madhav). It excludes the Gandhi-era Akhand Hindustan of Munshi and the secular reunification calls of figures like Katju. Economic and social questions are mostly inferred from the wider Sangh family.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a core concern of the idea; Sangh-family parties accept a welfare role for the state, so an adherent leans mildly in favour.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The concept says nothing on wages and Sangh-family economics (swadeshi, anti-socialist) pulls both ways.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Golwalkar's slogan was 'not socialism but Hinduism' and Jana Sangh was economic-nationalist, so adherents are split between market and state emphasis.

public-ownership.rationale: Jana Sangh combined economic nationalism with decentralisation of industry; no settled line on public ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Akhand Bharat is a territorial-civilisational claim and does not address tax rates.

unions-good.rationale: Sangh-linked labour thinking prefers class cooperation to class conflict, but unions as such are not addressed by the concept.

property-fundamental.rationale: Golwalkar's anti-communism made the movement friendly to property owners; inferred rather than stated for this concept.

regulate-corporations.rationale: No stated position; swadeshi economic nationalism and pro-business leanings offset each other.

cut-welfare.rationale: The concept does not address welfare and adherents have no shared line.

worker-ownership.rationale: The movement's anti-socialist stance ('not socialism but Hinduism') suggests rejection of collective ownership models.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Hard line on Pakistan and security in the Jana Sangh programme implies acceptance of security measures; inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Cultural conservatism of Hindutva makes drug legalisation unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents are split: they resist speech limits aimed at Hindu groups but favour limits on speech seen as offending Hindu sentiment.

strong-leader.rationale: Concept is about territory; adherents work within parliamentary politics and the movement has not made leader-supremacy central.

state-harmful.rationale: The concept demands a large unified state; the ideology is statist and nationalist, so rejecting the state is far from it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed by the concept; no documented split or shared line among adherents.

empower-police-military.rationale: Jana Sangh supported nuclear armament and a tough line on Pakistan and China, implying strong security forces.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Cultural conservatism implies opposition; not explicitly documented.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not addressed by the concept; no stable position.

traditional-family.rationale: Jana Sangh manifestos described the joint family and indissoluble marriage as the basis of Hindu society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Sangh-family organisations have generally resisted it as contrary to tradition, though views vary; inferred.

abortion-legal.rationale: Cultural conservatism suggests mild opposition; not a documented core issue.

more-religion-public.rationale: Savarkar's Hindutva makes culture and a holy land central to nationhood, though he separated Hindutva from ritual religion, so support is moderate.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Hindutva writers frame preferential redress as divisive of Hindu unity, though caste uplift is accepted by some; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Traditionalist view of gender roles implies rejection; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Culture (sanskriti) is one of the three pillars of Hindutva and the concept rests on a civilisational homeland.

gradual-change.rationale: Adherents want a reversal of Partition but say it should come through popular goodwill, while also stressing national rebirth.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Golwalkar and Savarkar treat Muslims and Christians as outsiders; Sangh politics backs tighter control of migration from Bangladesh.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Civilisational nationalism puts sovereignty first; no direct statement on the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Jana Sangh was economic-nationalist yet had no stable trade position; the concept does not address trade.

nation-first.rationale: The concept ranks the civilisational nation above present state frontiers and Jana Sangh pursued an independent foreign policy.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' frame is civilisational unity, not human-rights intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Adherents reject the present borders only to merge the subcontinent into one state; a world of open borders contradicts the Hindu-nation basis.

limit-growth.rationale: Economic nationalists favour production growth (Jana Sangh called for more food and cloth).

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not addressed by the concept.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Jana Sangh backed nuclear armament, and the party's nuclear stance extends naturally to power; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Supporters say reunification should come by popular goodwill, not revolution; the movement works through elections.

experts-over-public.rationale: The concept concerns territory, and the Sangh family is electorally populist rather than technocratic, so no stance is documented.

central-planning.rationale: Golwalkar's anti-socialist slogan implies rejection of central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Anti-socialist stance rules out public or worker ownership as a basis for markets; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: No Sangh-family source ties Akhand Bharat or Hindutva to a single land tax; no position can be inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation never appears in Hindutva programmes; the movement defends family continuity but has no stated tax line.

basic-income.rationale: An unconditional state income is absent from Jana Sangh and RSS programmes; adherents have no shared view.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Jana Sangh was an economic-nationalist party; inferred support for protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Economic nationalism suggests some support but adherents are split and nothing is stated for this concept.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Jana Sangh's decentralisation of industry and integral humanism point mildly this way; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Directly opposed to communist abolition of wages; Golwalkar named communists as enemies.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; a nationalist-statist outlook implies rejection.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Integral humanism has organic-society themes, yet state-recognised wage bodies are not part of the Akhand Bharat claim.

one-party-rule.rationale: Sangh-family politics operates in multiparty elections; Jana Sangh was an opposition party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Savarkar spoke of a Hindu empire but modern adherents accept republican government.

democracy-best.rationale: The RSS in 1949 adopted loyalty to the Indian Constitution; Sangh-family bodies compete in elections.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums on laws are not part of the Jana Sangh programme, and the concept itself is about territorial unity.

workers-councils.rationale: Anti-communist; councils as the basis of power are alien to it.

right-to-secede.rationale: The concept aims to undo the Partition and Hindutva opposes separatism, so regional secession is rejected.

natural-rulers.rationale: Golwalkar defended caste order but modern adherents deny hereditary rule claims; they are split.

political-violence-never.rationale: Savarkar praised valour and 'fire and sword', and Godse invoked Akhand Bharat, so adherents do not hold violence never justified, though the mainstream now insists on peaceful means.

war-builds-character.rationale: Savarkar glorifies martial valour while mainstream modern adherents do not claim war is good for character.

separate-church-state.rationale: Hindutva rejects Congress-style secularism as favouring minorities; Hindu culture is to underpin the state.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Savarkar separated Hindutva from religion and was an atheist; Hindutva is cultural, not scripture-based law, though Golwalkar praised Manu.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Strong state, military and defence are core to the idea.

military-superiority.rationale: Jana Sangh backed nuclear arms and a tough line on Pakistan and China.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Savarkar grounded the Hindu nation on common blood and culture, though the definition is inclusive of converts and wider than a single ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hindutva rejects Marxism; Golwalkar named communists as internal enemies.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Anti-socialist and caste-order-defending strands oppose equality of outcome.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Hindutva claims Hindus as the indigenous people of the subcontinent, but the statement is framed for other contexts; split.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Adherents resent colonialism but have no reparations programme.

civilizational-union.rationale: Akhand Bharat is exactly this: one civilisational unit from Afghanistan to Myanmar to be united.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Duty and nation-centred ethics oppose valuing self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Golwalkar subordinated individuals and minorities to the nation; the RSS stresses duty to the nation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Hindu reverence for rivers and the sacred land exists, but no source ties it to this ideology politically.

limit-population.rationale: Adherents are split, some alarmed at Muslim demographic growth and some opposed to coercion.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Jana Sangh wanted increased production; not anti-industrial.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Disruptive acceleration is not on the agenda of a movement that stresses heritage and rebirth of an older order.

human-enhancement.rationale: Transhumanist questions are untouched by the concept, and cultural conservatives would be wary but have not ruled.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The idea predates and ignores algorithmic governance; no adherent position is documented.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A security-minded movement leans against it, but no source states a view, so the answer stays neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: Reuniting a lost civilisational homeland rests on restoring an older order, though adherents also speak of progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Committed ideologues of Hindutva put ideology first.

direct-action.rationale: Supporters say reunification should come through popular goodwill and electoral politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: Supporters say popular goodwill should drive reunification, yet Savarkar celebrated force, so adherents are split on the principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed to it; the movement stresses production and national strength.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Golwalkar defended caste and functional order; Marxist abolition is rejected.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist principle; rejected by an anti-socialist movement.

production-for-use.rationale: Communist slogan; rejected by an anti-socialist movement.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist claim; Golwalkar was anti-communist and popular with business supporters.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Direct opposite of Hindutva; communists were named internal enemies.

collective-farming.rationale: Anti-communist; Jana Sangh favoured decentralised production and smallholdings.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist thesis; rejected by the anti-communist movement.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement is statist and nationalist, so it rejects the idea.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; some adherents support moral restrictions beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Golwalkar subordinated individual and minority rights to the Hindu nation; group identity is central.

conscription.rationale: Strong defence emphasis implies acceptance; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; nation-centred outlook ranks voice and belonging above exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; a statist-nationalist outlook rejects treating citizens as customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Debates on freedom as material capacity are foreign to the sources, which treat liberty in national terms.

media-academia-power.rationale: Hindutva sources complain of liberal elite bias; documented but not specific to this concept.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Savarkar spoke of common blood but did not make racial genetics hierarchy central; split.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; some integral-humanism thinkers favoured organic views.

total-state.rationale: Jana Sangh wanted decentralisation and the Sangh stresses society over state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Supporters present Akhand Bharat as completing national awakening, per Bhagwat's remark that only a united society brings real freedom.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The concept is irredentist: it seeks to unify neighbouring territories into a single state, and some followers press claims on Pakistan-administered Kashmir.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern electoral politics; oaths of personal loyalty as basis of authority do not apply.

bound-labor.rationale: Not endorsed in any modern programme.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Hindutva writers do claim a bias in academia against them, but the epistemological thesis is not an Akhand Bharat position.

universal-morality.rationale: Not addressed; Hindutva stresses cultural particularity, which pulls against universalism.

single-common-good.rationale: The Hindu nation is presented as one organic whole with a single national interest; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Jana Sangh manifesto called for full relations with Israel; Hindutva ideologues have sympathised with Zionism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Savarkar's Hindu nation extends to Hindus everywhere, so a right of return for diaspora members follows; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Savarkar championed Hindusthani as the language of Hindusthan, and Jana Sangh pushed Hindi as the national tongue.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Anti-socialist stance; democratic control of firms is not favoured.

school-vouchers.rationale: School choice funding is not part of the Jana Sangh programme or the territorial concept.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed by Akhand Bharat, and Sangh-family parties have varied in practice.

economic-freedom.rationale: Golwalkar was anti-socialist, but Jana Sangh also favoured economic nationalism, so adherents do not agree on this link.

rule-by-example.rationale: Golwalkar and RSS stress personal character in cadres, yet governing by example in place of law is not a stated doctrine.

national-self-determination.rationale: Adherents treat the subcontinent as one nation and reject self-determination for separate states carved from it; the statement is ambiguous for them.

force-without-un.rationale: Strong defence line and nationalism suggest independence from UN approval; inferred from Jana Sangh's hard line on Pakistan.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Savarkar was rationalist about religion while the movement stresses emotion and heritage; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Golwalkar denied non-Hindu foreigners privileges; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Welfare conditionality is not discussed in the sources; no stance can be inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hindutva sets 'not socialism but Hinduism' against class struggle and stresses national unity.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Hindutva is built on heritage and civilisation; sacrificing it is contrary.

dominated-front.rationale: Not a stated theme; Indian Sangh politics pursues an independent line rather than a bloc against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: Hindutva organises labour along national lines against Marxist internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Traditional family and gender order; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury bans are not found in Hindutva sources and Jana Sangh favoured production and trade, so no clear lean.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Jana Sangh's programme promised equal rights regardless of caste, community or creed; legal racial segregation is not a position.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is outside the concept; Jana Sangh wanted more production generally, but nothing specific.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Golwalkar said foreign races must merge into the Hindu culture or stay subordinate.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not an Akhand Bharat position; fringe Hindutva demographic claims exist but are not defining.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral system design is not discussed in the sources; Sangh-family parties have worked within first-past-the-post.

national-mission.rationale: Supporters present India as holding a civilisational mission; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Hindutva writers deny structural male dominance; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Jana Sangh opposed the Congress establishment; mild.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic limits on reproduction are not in the sources; Golwalkar praised German racial policy toward Jews, but not this policy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nationalist, pro-security outlook resists accountability; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The movement is statist and nationalist and wants an expansive unified state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Savarkar's blood-community theory is inclusive of converts and no programme exists; split.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Official Jana Sangh programme promised equal rights, yet Golwalkar denied citizens' rights to minorities who refused assimilation; split.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Marxist question; the movement rejects socialism altogether.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Hindutva rejects colonial characterisation of states and views Zionism sympathetically.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Jana Sangh's 1967 manifesto promised a uniform law on marriage, succession and adoption for all citizens.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Hindutva favours bans on conversion; Savarkar treated those who leave Hindu culture as lost to the nation.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Jana Sangh campaigned for a nationwide ban in the early 1960s.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Hindutva seeks cultural content in state education; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist question; not applicable, so adherents have no view.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Supporters say reunification should come by popular goodwill, implying consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Jana Sangh was economic-nationalist, which could favour exporting, but no source states a surplus target.

population-transfer.rationale: Golwalkar suggested minorities stay subordinate; the official movement rejects expulsion and fringe voices differ.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Savarkar glorified fire and sword and Hindus conquering; absolute pacifism is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Savarkar admired martial struggle between peoples; mainstream adherents split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The 1948 ban on the RSS taught caution but Sangh sources favour banning separatists; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: This republican concept is absent from Hindutva writing, so no position can be documented.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional checks are not discussed in the sources, though the RSS accepted the Indian Constitution in 1949.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Integral humanism's concern for the poorest is Sangh-family but not defining for this concept.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing policy question with no connection to the concept or Indian Sangh-family programmes.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law rules are not in the sources; Sangh-linked unions pursue cooperation but have no stated position on ballots.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Hindutva writers raise demography chiefly in communal terms; no source ties population to poverty causation.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Golwalkar and Savarkar argued that a single culture is needed for nationhood.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; alien to the movement's electoral politics.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Its hard security line favours strong powers against enemies, but there is no documented position on suspending legal protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Jana Sangh wanted more food production, but price fixing in scarcity is not documented as a position.

party-controls-media.rationale: Jana Sangh operated as an opposition party that would favour media freedom; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: Jana Sangh was a multiparty-system party and supported a strong national army under the state, not the party.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay caps for legislators are not part of the sources; the idea belongs to socialist traditions.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Cadre-style organisation of the Sangh family; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Adherents want union of the subcontinent in a single state, not a supranational pooling, though Advani floated an India-Pakistan confederation in 2004.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The sources document no view on executive versus legislative control of the forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Hierarchical church governance is a Christian question and Savarkar treated Christians as outsiders, so there is no position.

clerical-rule.rationale: Savarkar was an atheist and Hindutva is cultural-political, not clerical.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Cultural conservatism supports some censorship; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not addressed in Hindutva or Akhand Bharat sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall elections do not appear in the Jana Sangh programme or the concept.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Jana Sangh favoured independence in foreign policy but not specifically dropping alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; alien to the movement.

people-in-arms.rationale: Savarkar urged militarisation of Hindus yet the modern state army is accepted; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Sangh sources stress Hindu village heritage, but a claim of rural moral superiority is not documented.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Hindutva writers attack liberal academia, yet the sources do not generalise to graduates as such.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Hindutva holds Hindu civilisation as the national core and distinguishes cultures from outsiders; relativism is not its stance.

death-penalty.rationale: Hard line on terrorism and Pakistan; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Hindutva has promoted Vedic science claims, but teaching creationism specifically is not a documented position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Savarkar's definition rests on common blood and ancestral land.

minority-language-support.rationale: Savarkar and Jana Sangh favoured one national language; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Opposes separate religion-based law, consistent with the Uniform Civil Code position.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity to national culture is stressed over eccentric ways of living; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt relief is outside the concept, and Sangh-family parties have no stated position.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Hindu nationalists framed independence politically and culturally, and Jana Sangh opposed socialism, so no lean emerges.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The idea is territorial; the Sangh family works within the existing Constitution, so rewriting is not a stated aim.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Jana Sangh sought growth but within parliamentary democracy, and no source endorses trading freedoms for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Global aid duties are not addressed by the concept, which is nation-centred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Jana Sangh supported nuclear armament; Hindutva favours strategic autonomy.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidential election mode is not discussed in the sources.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The defining aim: reversing Partition and unifying a subcontinent split by the British-drawn division.

decide-locally.rationale: A single reunified state is the aim, and Jana Sangh pressed full integration of Kashmir, so local primacy is disfavoured.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The concept is silent on technology; adherents mix modernising nationalism with cultural traditionalism.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The idea is territorial and civilisational and says nothing on monetary policy; Sangh-family economics pulls both ways.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Akhand Bharat holds the subcontinent to be one sacred homeland, and the Jana Sangh programme opposed concessions on Kashmir and territory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh family stresses duty to the nation and community over individualism, though it is not anti-property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Inferred: Golwalkar and the Sangh were anti-communist but the idea takes no position on whether the USSR was socialist or state capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; Sangh-family parties have no common line.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; Sangh-family views on formal alliances are mixed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred: the Jana Sangh programme demanded full integration of Kashmir, implying unconsented-to or contested control is not legitimate, though adherents apply this selectively.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva writers object to state control of Hindu temples and see religion as the nation core, so adherents lean against subordinating religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred: a head of state as a unifying national symbol fits the civilisational nation, but the idea does not address it.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Hindutva and the Jana Sangh oppose separatism and call for a united India, supporting force to keep a region in the state.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The Jana Sangh programme opposed special status for Kashmir and wanted full integration under one system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred: Hindu nationalism treats kingship as bound by dharma rather than as divine, and modern Sangh parties accept secular office.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; Sangh-family economics pulls both ways.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred: the Hindu tradition holds that the king is bound by dharma, and Sangh parties work within a constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred: Sangh-family governments back space and nuclear programmes as national strength, though the idea does not address it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents split.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred: the RSS stresses organization over personalities, so open leader worship runs against its stated culture.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; adherents split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Golwalkar and the Sangh family were militantly anti-communist, so an adherent rejects the Marxist-Leninist claim.

land-redistribution.rationale: The concept is territorial; Jana Sangh economics gave no settled line on breaking up estates. Inferred, so neutral.

refugee-return.rationale: Partition displaced millions, and Sangh-family writers want the displaced and their kin able to return to a reunited land. Inferred from the reunification aim.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The claim rests on a shared civilisational homeland and Hindu nation rather than on co-nationals alone, but it does rest on culture and kinship across the borders.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Hindutva opposes conversion away from Hinduism but does not call for legal punishment of leaving a religion; inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Sangh-family writers criticise compulsory religious dress codes, though not on liberal grounds; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Reunification would create one state with one currency, but a currency union among separate states is not something the concept addresses.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Savarkar defined the Hindu nation by common land, blood and culture, which supports unity of kin peoples across present borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Golwalkar wanted minorities absorbed into one Hindu national culture, not given self-governing institutions of their own.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The concept treats the whole subcontinent as the Hindu homeland, so the dilemma of founding one elsewhere does not map onto it; adherents are split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Hindutva ideology is culture- and civilisation-centred, not a materialist theory of history; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed by the concept or the Jana Sangh programme.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed by the concept; no settled Sangh-family line.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Golwalkar held that the majority nation defines the state, which sits uneasily with courts overriding it; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed by the concept; Sangh-family positions are mixed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Jana Sangh stressed swadeshi and economic nationalism, which leans toward self-reliance, though not a closed bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: Sangh-family thought stresses duty (dharma) and sacrifice over material reward; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Savarkar's circle admired armed revolutionaries, but the modern mainstream says reunification should come by goodwill, so adherents are split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed by the concept; Sangh-family views on privilege are mixed (opposed untouchability, but not clearly hereditary titles).

history-own-civilization.rationale: Hindutva places the Hindu nation and its civilisation at the centre of its account of history.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Hindu nationalism grew in opposition to British rule, so rule over others for their benefit is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Hindutva and the Sangh family stress national pride and loyalty to Bharat Mata as educational aims.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Sangh-family adherents split on reservations, with the question mostly about caste; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: Sangh-family economics, swadeshi and anti-socialist, do not call for state money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred from the Sangh family's anti-socialist, market-leaning economics.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Akhand Bharat itself is a claim to cultural and political unity across the lands of the subcontinent.

delink-world-market.rationale: Swadeshi favours national self-reliance but not a break with the world economy; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The Sangh family rejects class-struggle thinking, so it does not hold the labour-aristocracy thesis; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred: Sangh-family communitarian outlook accepts anti-discrimination law in principle; Jana Sangh programme demands uniform civil law.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Savarkar and Golwalkar emphasise the Hindu nation over constitutional limits; adherents split, inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: Sangh narratives treat Partition as a colonial imposition on a united land.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva accepts electoral politics; Savarkar did not require a hereditary ruler.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: Sangh organisational ideology stresses unity and discipline over individual dissent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: dharma tradition holds that a ruler who breaks dharma may be resisted.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: the Jana Sangh programme worked through Parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: Hindu tradition emphasises compassion to living beings (ahimsa).

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: cow protection and vegetarian values in the Sangh family oppose killing animals for food.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: seva and dharma teach duty toward the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh family demands active civic and national participation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva does not address mass-culture critique.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva has no doctrine on hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: swadeshi and anti-colonial narratives blame colonial extraction for poverty.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: Savarkar defines the nation by fatherland and holy land, favouring natives over outsiders.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh opposes foreign direction of Indian politics.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: swadeshi and self-reliance (Atmanirbhar) are Sangh themes.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Reversing the 1947 Partition and recovering lost territories is the defining aim of Akhand Bharat.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva claims Hindus as the indigenous people of the land and Muslim rule as foreign.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: Sangh family treats anti-fascism as a left-wing frame.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh is strongly anti-communist.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: Akhand Bharat has no stake in the question.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: Sangh campaigns rename places and remove symbols of Mughal and colonial rule.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: socially conservative; men's rights groups in India find a hearing in the Sangh family.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred: Golwalkar and the Sangh seek institutions rooted in Bharatiya civilisation, not Western models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred: Sangh doctrine accepts civilian democratic rule.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: Sangh doctrine treats home and family duties as dharma rather than paid labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Sangh-family thought stresses duty to family and elders as part of Hindu cultural values; inferred, not stated in the sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: The concept says nothing on civil-service selection; adherents have no settled view.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Jana Sangh was economic-nationalist and swadeshi, so blocking foreign control of key industries is inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Sangh-family social conservatism and Hindu marriage norms lean against easy divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Sangh family works through parliamentary party politics and disciplined leadership, not instructed delegates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; Jana Sangh economics mixed swadeshi with a state welfare role, so adherents are split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Jana Sangh and the wider family defend private property (see property-fundamental); communal land tenure is inferred to be rejected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Jana Sangh contested parliamentary elections and accepted constitutional democracy, so legislative control of the budget is inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Hindutva texts and the Jana Sangh pushed a common national language (Hindi/Hindusthani) as part of national unity; inferred from the programme.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land as the sacred homeland of the Hindu nation implies keeping it in citizens' hands; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Consistent with the audit's rejection of correcting racial injustice; the family treats group-outcome remedies as divisive.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Swadeshi and simple-living themes pull one way, aspiration and growth the other; no settled view.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Mainstream Akhand Bharat says reunification should come by goodwill, yet the family is hawkish toward Pakistan; adherents are split.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The mainstream stresses reunification by popular goodwill rather than force, so imposing by troops on allies is inferred to be rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed; no settled Sangh-family position.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva concern about foreign-funded missionary and NGO influence.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: Sangh favoured integrating all regions under national law, as in ending special status.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the Jana Sangh's market and swadeshi leanings over state guarantees.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the idea concerns civilisational unity rather than regime type.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Inferred from Golwalkar's organic view of the nation over individual consent.

non-intervention.rationale: Reunifying neighbouring states implies a claim over their affairs; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Savarkar's test of loyalty treats Muslims and Christians as having a holy land abroad, feeding suspicion of divided allegiance.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva support for traditional marriage.

local-production.rationale: Inferred from the Jana Sangh's swadeshi economic outlook.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Sangh family is a disciplined organization and party structure.

religious-nation.rationale: Hindutva defines the nation by Hindu culture, land and heritage.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's assertion of Indian civilisational primacy, which rejects submission to any foreign power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from Jana Sangh's unitary national outlook, which favours central pooling.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh family opposes collectivism and Marxist common ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: Golwalkar and the Jana Sangh treated communism as a major threat.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from Jana Sangh's openness to private enterprise alongside state welfare.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Sangh economics, with swadeshi and integral humanism, praises neither capitalism nor socialism; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's traditional family and gender outlook.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's emphasis on the traditional family.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Savarkar championed a Sanskritised Hindusthani over foreign-derived vocabulary; inferred as the movement's tendency.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the movement's unitary-state nationalism.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh favours a unitary nation over self-governing cooperative communities.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from Jana Sangh's push to integrate Kashmir and other regions.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred from the Jana Sangh's integral humanism, a third course between capitalism and communism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Savarkar defines the Hindu nation by a common fatherland and holy land, and Akhand Bharat rests on a civilisational tie to the whole subcontinent over present borders.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred that a committed adherent accepts the established account of the Holocaust.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Sangh-family opinion has been split between social conservatism and more recent acceptance of decriminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh family works within electoral democracy, though Golwalkar's writings show authoritarian leanings on minorities and order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: Savarkar's Hindutva is cultural and nationalist rather than a call for the state to punish other religions.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from anti-British nationalism; the idea is about reuniting the homeland, not ruling overseas territories for profit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: a Muslim religious duty that adherents, who treat Islam as an outside force, would not endorse.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva aims at a Hindu nation, not government by religious law, and Savarkar was no theocrat.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; the Sangh family has both village-level self-rule themes and a hierarchical organisational style.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva frames society through the unified Hindu nation, not intersecting identity-based oppressions.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative Sangh family outlook.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the socially conservative Sangh family outlook; the idea itself does not address it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Inferred: Jana Sangh's Integral Humanism claimed a path beyond both capitalism and communism.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: Golwalkar and the Sangh family were strongly anti-communist and reject Marxian labour theory.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Golwalkar treats non-Hindu minorities as outsiders to the nation, so adherents lean to agree Islam sits poorly with Hindu culture; the Western context is inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: Savarkar grounds the nation in land, blood and culture rather than divine authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; Sangh-family states have restricted hijabs in schools while defending Hindu symbols, so adherents are split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed by the idea; inferred as indifferent.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: Jana Sangh favoured a mixed economy with state welfare and swadeshi, short of laissez-faire or full state control.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Savarkar's martial themes and the Jana Sangh programme of nuclear armament make a strong military central to the idea.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from Jana Sangh's Antyodaya emphasis on helping the poorest first rather than letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Jana Sangh was anti-Soviet and pro-Israel yet defended Indian independence of action; adherents are split on alignment.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Sangh-family politicians routinely attack hereditary party leadership, so an adherent leans against hereditary office; inferred, not a stated Akhand Bharat position.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Sangh economic tradition (swadeshi, integral humanism) never adopted mutual banking; inferred that adherents lean to ordinary banking or state credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Swadeshi economic self-reliance is a Sangh-family theme, so an adherent leans toward rejecting externally imposed conditions; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: The Jana Sangh programme operated under universal adult suffrage and the Hindu nation is defined by culture and land, not wealth; inferred.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminism is not part of the Hindutva framework, which stresses civilisational and national unity over this analysis; inferred.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-derived concept alien to Hindutva, whose critique of capitalism rests on cultural and national grounds; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Hindutva does not make this class critique of formal freedoms; inferred from the Jana Sangh's acceptance of constitutional liberties.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Jana Sangh programme stood within the constitutional order and rule of law; inferred rather than stated for Akhand Bharat itself.

racial-franchise.rationale: Golwalkar-era texts demanded subordinate status for non-Hindus (s4) while the mainstream Sangh today claims equal citizenship; the idea defines the nation by culture and land, so adherents are split.

online-participation.rationale: Sangh-family governments promote digital governance, so an adherent leans in favour; inferred, not stated by the idea.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the Sangh family's support for digital governance and transparency in government; the idea itself says nothing on it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Hindutva-linked bodies back restricting interfaith marriage, such as anti-conversion and 'love jihad' laws, to protect the Hindu community; the idea itself is territorial.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Some Sangh-affiliated groups have urged such boycotts but the mainstream leadership disowns them and the idea itself is territorial, so adherents are split.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sangh-family politics rests on mass organisation, elections and a cultural leadership, not on sortition; inferred from that, so an adherent leans against it.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Savarkar urged a rationalist, reformist Hindu society and Hinduism has no single medieval authority to preserve, so adherents lean towards updating; inferred from his writings, but Sangh traditionalists dissent.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Sangh family stresses cultural unity over class and has supported business-friendly parties; Golwalkar was anti-communist, so adherents would not see wealth as a threat to liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Hindutva organisations have been socially conservative and the RSS long resisted decriminalisation, though some voices have softened; inferred from the wider Sangh family.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Savarkar and Golwalkar built the nation on Hindu culture and sacred land, so a state campaign against religion is opposed to the core of Hindutva.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Hindutva stresses a strong state, order and national security, and the Jana Sangh programme was security-minded, so abolition is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Golwalkar's Hindu Rashtra and Savarkar's Hindutva reject guaranteed communal shares of power as a legacy of Partition-era communal politics.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Sangh family runs large service and charity networks and values seva and community, though the Jana Sangh also accepted a state welfare role; leaning yes, inferred.

term-limits.rationale: The idea says nothing on office tenure and Sangh-family parties have long-serving leaders; inferred as mildly against limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Hindutva favours a strong unified national parliamentary state and never raises delegable voting, so it is inferred as unwelcome.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The idea never addresses extinction risk; adherents have no clear lean and put national unity first, so neutral is inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Hindu priesthood and Sangh leadership have been largely male, though Sangh groups have women's wings; adherents are split and the answer is inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Sangh-family thought praises women as mothers and keepers of tradition but also accepts equality in law; adherents are split and this is inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: Sangh thinking ties political membership to Hindutva's fatherland-and-holy-land test, so foreigners voting is unlikely to be favoured; not discussed in the sources.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the Sangh family's property and market orientation; no source covers rent control.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred: Sangh economic policy has favoured domestic enterprise and swadeshi, but has not called for abolishing IP; not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The RSS runs drilled, uniformed shakhas for boys and young men to build discipline and national character, as the Sangh family's core organising method.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred: Sangh nationalism supports India's nuclear arsenal as a deterrent, though the question of foreign weapons on Indian soil is separate; no source addresses it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from nationalist insistence on sovereignty and the Jana Sangh's non-alignment tendencies; sources do not address bases directly.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva writers stress the Partition killings and the Mughal-era persecution of Hindus, and would back formal recognition of such mass killings.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the Jana Sangh programme and Hindutva's reformist economic thinking, not stated explicitly in the sources.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: Hindu nationalists honour armed defence and the soldier, and Savarkar held violence legitimate for the nation; no source discusses pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Savarkar and Golwalkar describe the Hindu nation as continuous from the Vedic period to the present, and Akhand Bharat is built on civilisational unity from antiquity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva generally holds to a traditional, biological view of sex and gender, though the sources do not address it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh family holds a traditional view of woman's role and does not endorse deconstructing the category; not discussed in the sources.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: Hindu nationalism honours those killed for the nation, using the language of 'balidan' and martyr (shaheed), though 'saints' is a stretch.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Hindutva joins religion and politics, and Golwalkar treats the nation as spiritual, but the good-versus-evil framing is not stated in the sources; adherents split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Akhand Bharat wants the homeland gathered into one state, not just a cultural centre; inferred from the reunification aim.

culture-before-state.rationale: Golwalkar and the RSS put cultural and civilisational revival of the Hindu nation first, with state-building following, though the Jana Sangh also entered politics.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva generally follows the tradition of male-language divinity though many Hindus hold God beyond gender; not addressed.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh family defends tradition and has not made judging scripture by women's humanity a principle; not addressed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Hindutva makes Hindus the national community and the Jana Sangh pressed for national control of economic life, though specifically 'majority rather than minorities' is inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: The Akhand Bharat aim itself is to merge the subcontinent's states into one country for one civilisational people, reversing Partition.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: Sangh-family organisations present their labour wing as independent of political parties.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: Hindutva rejects class-struggle frames in favour of a civilisational nation, so workers' power is not the test of legitimate society.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: Sangh-family parties accept public provision of basic services.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred: the idea says nothing on legislative structure.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: Sangh-family economic thought favours private and national ownership over local communal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The idea seeks one integral nation, and Jana Sangh favoured a unitary state, so delegate-only confederations are rejected.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: Sangh-family traditionalism supports family-centred social order.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; modernising nationalist economics is mildly favourable.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: nationalist governance favours state visibility of finance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: no stated position; Sangh-family governments have favoured identifiable online activity.

person-over-state.rationale: Hindutva and Golwalkar place the nation and its culture above the individual.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Hindutva rests on a shared sacred geography and culture, with spiritual life treated as central.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: Jana Sangh favoured a unitary India, so regional powers rest on the national legislature.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred: Sangh-family swadeshi groups have opposed genetically modified crops.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Savarkar's Hindutva defines the nation partly through common blood and race (jati), so group organisation is supported.

racial-pride.rationale: Savarkar celebrates the common blood and heritage of the Hindu people.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: the idea is irredentist and some adherents accept force, though the mainstream says goodwill, so a strict defensive-only rule is not held.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Sangh thinkers define the nation by shared land, culture and Hindu civilisation, not by language, and distrust linguistic politics; Savarkar's Hindutva rests on fatherland and holy land.

communal-electorates.rationale: Hindu nationalists have opposed separate electorates since the Partition era, which they blame on them; Jana Sangh called for a uniform national identity.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Akhand Bharat holds that Partition was an artificial division, and Sangh writers blame British policy and the Muslim League for it.

free-public-college.rationale: The Sangh family has no settled line on tuition; inferred from a mixed record of state and private education.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from the Sangh's economic nationalism and a stress on development over new taxes, not from stated doctrine.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the civilisational and sacred view of the motherland that the sources describe, which implies an inherited duty.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh family often honours women as embodiments of the motherland and of cultural values, though sources do not state it.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from the Sangh's emphasis on military strength and national security, and its irredentist aim.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh family has favoured strong state security and had no commitment to open diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: The Jana Sangh favoured swadeshi self-reliance but later Sangh parties liberalised; the family is split.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the Sangh family's nationalism and respect for the army; it also has a tradition of armed self-defence.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Savarkar and Golwalkar prize military strength and duty to the nation, so refusing orders in war runs against the position.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: the Sangh's Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh favours unions, but within a class-collaboration frame.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred; the sources do not discuss it and the Jana Sangh programme had no settled line on it.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred; the sources do not discuss fiscal rules and adherents have no common line.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the Sangh's swadeshi, self-reliance economics, which resists the existing international order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement aims at an organic unified nation-state, not the destruction of the state's machinery.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the Sangh's insistence on one national culture and civilisational order, which leaves little room for varied systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The sources do not discuss it; the Sangh reveres the land but has no common line on pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Savarkar's Hindutva makes the motherland and holy land the centre of a nation that outlasts its members; Golwalkar calls the nation a living being.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred; student debt relief is not a Sangh or Jana Sangh demand and adherents have no common line.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the movement's view of the subcontinent as one nation, which denies a colonial split between regions.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Hindutva's dharmic outlook, which holds duties follow from a shared human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: The sources do not discuss it and adherents hold no common line.

missingStatements.text: The Indian subcontinent's present states should be reunited into a single country.
missingStatements.rationale: The defining Akhand Bharat aim, held by RSS and Jana Sangh since Partition; the nearest existing statement is only about divided nations in general.

missingStatements.text: The sacred land of a nation's religion should lie within its own borders.
missingStatements.rationale: Savarkar's test of a Hindu is that India is both fatherland and holy land, which he used to set Muslims and Christians apart.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Hindu nationalist doctrine of the holy land; too narrow and not a question many ideologies would take sides on.

missingStatements.text: Cultural unity of a civilisation justifies redrawing the political borders of present nation-states.
missingStatements.rationale: Golwalkar and RSS leaders place civilisational boundaries above today's frontiers.

notes: Many economic and social answers are low-confidence inferences from the Sangh family, since Akhand Bharat itself is a territorial claim. Adherents split on whether reunification is purely cultural or political, and on peaceful versus forceful means; the mainstream says peaceful.
